packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no identification was revealed to me in context beforehand)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context proposed an identification of this text. I have not tried to identify work or author.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

The packet shows two faces of one parchment leaf, mounted on a modern paper guard.
- Face A: overview image-001; tiles image-002 .. image-007.
- Face B: overview image-008; tiles image-009 .. image-014.

Observations:
- Upright orientation, two columns per face, about 31 written lines per column. No running title visible, no rubric in red script. Ruling/prickings visible in the intercolumn and margins.
- Script: a rounded minuscule, brown ink, words often run together; "&" used inside words (hab&, cer&); punctuation "·;" and "·" ; abbreviation "&cr" for et cetera.
- Sentence initials slightly enlarged and touched/filled with orange-red on Face B (C, Q, N, L, A, D, V, H, S). No large decorated initial. No interlinear gloss seen. No underlining in the medieval text.
- Face A carries later (early modern) additions written over the medieval text in darker ink, upper half: a row of years "1574 - 1575 - 1576 - 1577 -", below "1578 - 1579", a large "A", "Chap(it)re d'aug[...]" (reading of the second word uncertain), "Conclusions" (uncertain), and "8 janvier 1574 — 27 juin 1579". Faint pen-trials at the very top edge (three times a word like "oyssian"/"possiau", unread). Modern pencil/ink foliation "6" top right. A round red ink stamp near the foot between the columns (legend unread). An ink blot between the columns.
- Damage: Face A left column has lost its left third to half (large losses filled with modern paper), and the surface is rubbed and faint throughout; Face B has losses along the outer (right) edge cutting line-ends of the right column, and mould staining at the foot. Lower outer corner cut diagonally.

Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous prose exposition in which short quoted lemmata (introduced after "·;" with a coloured capital, sometimes ended "&cr") alternate with explanatory comment (often opening "Ac si diceret", "Qui enim superius", "Hic datur intellegi", "Notandum uero"). Lemma and comment are in the same script and size; they are not visually distinguished except by the coloured initials.

Which face is recto and which verso is not determinable from the images alone; the content sequence suggests Face A precedes Face B, but I have not relied on that.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD

Selected: all four columns, line by line. Face B is read almost completely. Face A right column is read mostly; Face A left column only as line-ends (the beginnings are physically lost) and with many uncertain words.
Unread: later pen-trials at top of Face A; stamp legend; last 1-2 faint lines at the foot of both columns of Face A; several rubbed words noted below.
A raking-light or UV image of Face A would help; no adjacent crop is missing.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [lost] = parchment missing; line numbers count medieval text lines from the top of the named tile (later-hand lines on Face A are not counted). Tiles overlap; overlapping lines are given once and the second tile reference is noted.

7. LIMITATIONS

- Face A is abraded and overwritten by later notes; its left column lacks every line-beginning. Readings there marked "?" are weak, and in several places I can see letter-shapes without being able to resolve words. I have not filled these from sense.
- Face B right column loses line-ends to holes/tears from about line 1-3 and 11-18 and again at 27-31.
- Line counts per tile exclude later-hand lines and may be off by one where a tile cuts a line at top or bottom.
- Column order within each face (left then right) is assumed from normal practice; the order of the two faces is not established from the images.
- o/e, a/u and t/c confusions are possible in this script (e.g. "orbis"/"erbis", "homnib;").

Reader activity: opened READER2.md; PROMPT.md; image-001.jpg through image-014.jpg (all 14). I also ran one directory listing of the two packet directories (packet-01, packet-02) to see the image filenames, and read PROMPT.md before starting. packet.json was not opened.
